# Novel Features Brainstorm — valyu-pp-cli
**Run:** 20260619-151616-c25a2c3a | **Date:** 2026-06-19

---

## Customer model

**Persona 1 — Maya, RAG Infrastructure Engineer at a Series B AI startup**
Maya builds retrieval pipelines for an enterprise copilot. Her pain: she needs to evaluate search quality across different source combinations (web vs. proprietary vs. arXiv+PubMed) before committing to a source config for production. She runs dozens of test queries, compares result counts and costs, and has to manually track which config performed best. She also needs to budget per-query costs and alert if a search run exceeds a threshold.

**Persona 2 — Carlos, Quantitative Analyst at a mid-size hedge fund**
Carlos writes Python scripts that pull SEC filings, FRED economic data, and earnings news for a watchlist of 30 tickers. His pain: he runs the same multi-source searches weekly, manually stitches together results from different search types, and has no easy way to diff "what changed this week vs. last week" in the intelligence he collects. He wants a repeatable, scriptable research routine he can drop into a cron job.

**Persona 3 — Priya, Biotech Research Scientist at a drug discovery firm**
Priya monitors clinical trial status updates and new ChEMBL compound data for a target indication. Her pain: deep research tasks on a compound take 10-15 minutes; she submits one, forgets it, and has to manually check back. She also needs to extract and clean text from 20-30 PubMed abstracts and patent PDFs at once for downstream NLP. She wants fire-and-forget task submission with a notification-style output when results land.

**Persona 4 — Dev, Developer Advocate building a demo LLM agent**
Dev is writing a tutorial showing how to wire Valyu into a Claude-powered research agent. His pain: he needs to quickly demonstrate what Valyu returns for a given query — raw JSON, cost, sources cited — without writing Python boilerplate. He also wants to pipe search results directly into a `| claude` command to show grounded generation. He needs clean, composable output formats (JSON, plain text, newline-delimited URLs) for piping.

## Candidates (pre-cut)

**1. Search A/B comparison — side-by-side diff of two source configs for the same query** (source: a)

Run the same query against two different `--type` or `--sources` configs and print a unified diff of titles, URLs, and cost. Lets Maya evaluate whether `--type web` vs `--type paper` gives better recall for her RAG use case.

Kill/keep: No LLM dependency. Pure mechanical diff of two API responses. Feasible with two sequential search calls + local comparison. Keep.

Score estimate: Domain Fit 3 (core RAG evaluation pain), User Pain 3 (explicit from Maya), Build Feasibility 2 (two search calls + diff), Research Backing 1 = **9/10**

**2. Cost ledger — running tally of all search/answer/research API spend in a session or time window** (source: b)

Track cumulative cost across all CLI invocations using a local SQLite log. Output `valyu-pp-cli cost` with per-command breakdown, daily/weekly rollup, and alert if a configurable budget threshold is exceeded.

Kill/keep: No LLM dependency. Cost data comes from API responses. Local SQLite write on each call. Keep.

Score estimate: Domain Fit 2, User Pain 3 (pricing-based API, Carlos needs budget visibility), Build Feasibility 2, Research Backing 1 = **8/10**

**3. Watch mode — poll a deep research task until done, then write output file and print a summary line** (source: a)

`valyu-pp-cli research wait <task-id> --output report.md` already exists per manifest (#17). Reframe: `research watch` adds `--notify` (prints a bell/OS notification line) and `--interval` override, plus exits with code 0/1 for scripting. This is a thin wrapper on the existing wait command.

Kill/keep: Near-duplicate of manifest #17 `research wait`. The incremental value (exit code, interval flag) is too thin to be a separate feature. Kill — sibling is #17.

Kill/keep: No LLM dependency. Mechanical iteration over search calls. Local file I/O only. Different from `batch create` (which is DeepResearch batching). Keep.

**8. Answer with piped context — read additional context from stdin and inject into answer prompt** (source: a)

`cat my_notes.txt | valyu-pp-cli answer "What are the risks?" --inject-context` sends stdin content as additional context in the answer request. Dev can pipe prior search results into an answer call.

Kill/keep: Natural companion to feature #4 (batch search from file). No LLM dependency. Client-side accumulation of `cost` fields from responses. Merged into #4 as `--max-total-cost` flag.

Decision: merge into #4. Not a separate row.
